title: Domain pack
description: Plan 3. A pack manifest: activation evidence, constraints, reviewer guidance and tests. Packs attach by artifact and semantics, never by file extension alone, so 'activation' requires both an artifact kind and a semantic signal and a glob can only narrow a rule that already has them. Security, API and data facts are never dropped because a classifier was uncertain; the lookup path stays usable without one. A pack adds constraints and review lenses and never starts a lifecycle phase. Every attachment is recorded as an attachment_record ($defs/attachment_record) carrying the rationale for the selection. A pack manifest is configuration, not a durable run artifact, so it does not carry common's envelope.

project_scoped.description: Always false for the eight generic packs. Project facts (one client's tenancy model, integration boundaries or migration practice) belong to that project's KB rules and are never hardcoded into a globally shared pack (plan 3).

starts_phase.description: A pack never starts a lifecycle phase (plan 2.5, plan 3).

activation.description: Deterministic selection input. 'rules' each carry a stable id so an attachment_record can cite exactly which rule matched.

examples.description: Positive and negative activation evidence. Both directions are required: an example that must attach and an example that must not (plan 10, release scenario 1).

classifier_optional.description: True for every pack: the deterministic lookup path works with no classifier present, and an uncertain classifier never suppresses a match (plan 3).

constraints.description: What the pack adds to the work it attaches to. Each constraint cites the rule it comes from so a reviewer can check it rather than infer it.

authorization.description: A sensitive action this pack's work needs before it may proceed, e.g. dependency-add for pack-deps or public-contract-change for pack-api (plan 3, plan 7.2). Never granted by default.

reviewer_guidance.description: Which review lanes this pack sharpens and what it asks each one to look at. Guidance, not a new persona catalog: the pack never adds a seat that the review policy did not already permit (plan 6.1).

required_when_attached.description: True when attaching this pack makes the lane required, so its absence becomes an unavailable lane rather than a silent skip (plan 6.1, release scenario 3).

kb_rules.description: Where a project's own facts are read from, rather than embedded here (plan 3).

activation_rule.description: One activation rule. 'artifact_kinds' and 'semantics' are both required and both non-empty: a rule that could fire on a file extension alone is not expressible (plan 3). 'paths' may only narrow a rule that already matches on artifact and semantics.

semantics.description: What the change means, e.g. 'observable response shape changes', 'a trust boundary is crossed', 'a stated performance budget exists'.

paths.description: Optional narrowing only. Never sufficient on its own.

evidence_required.description: What the selector must actually observe before the rule fires, so a guess cannot stand in for the artifact.

attachment_record.description: What the attach-pack protocol writes when a pack attaches. Plan 3 requires the reason to be recorded, not reconstructable: 'rationale' and at least one matched rule id are mandatory, and 'rejected' keeps the packs that were considered and not attached so a later reader can see the selection was deliberate. A record never carries a grant; attaching a pack authorizes nothing (plan 2.5).

evidence.description: The artifacts and locations that satisfied the matched rules.

target.description: The ticket, review or run the pack attached to.

classifier_used.description: Recorded for transparency. A classifier's uncertainty is never a reason to drop a deterministic match (plan 3).

provenance.description: AGENTS.md, authoring rule 3. 'donor' means at least one adapted file with a provenance/adaptations.yaml row donor@commit:path that exists at the pin; 'conversation' carries a G:L locator instead of a fabricated source path (plan 1.4).
